label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: all complete True, pending max 4.0, failures 0, server errors 0.0, pool timeouts 0, other edges 0

report.summary: In the window, transfers were fast and error-free, and outbox delivery kept pace with arrivals. A static backlog of 138 FAILED outbox events predates the window and is unrelated to the transfer symptom.

findings.claim: Transfers showed no failures or multi-second latency: 0 server errors, p99 0.248 s, 422s only 41 of 621.
findings.reason: Complete coverage with 36/36 scrapes shows nothing matching the reported symptom.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery kept up: 541 arrivals vs 542 publications, all attempts succeeded at about 71 ms, mostly consumer auth time.
findings.reason: Arrivals and publications match per bucket, with no delivery errors or slow attempts.

findings.claim: 138 outbox events are stuck FAILED with a constant count, and the oldest undelivered age is 680-855 s and growing. They predate the window and no new failures occurred.
findings.reason: Failed stayed at 138 throughout while the age rose linearly, so it is an old residue, not an active fault.

findings.claim: The DB pool and locking were healthy: 0 acquisition timeouts, 0 pending borrowers, no blocking sessions.
findings.reason: The pool was never saturated and 90/90 blocker samples showed no blocking.

limitations: The window is only 3 minutes and does not cover when the customers experienced problems.
Blocker sampling is every 2 s and the pool gauges every 5 s, so brief events could be missed.
next_checks: Re-run over the time the customers reported failures or slow transfers.
Investigate why 138 outbox events became FAILED earlier, and what the oldest undelivered event is.

alternatives.reason: Only this window was observed, and it was clean.
alternatives.hypothesis: Intermittent customer-visible failures or slowness occurred outside this 3-minute window.

alternatives.reason: Their cause and timing are not visible here, and the transfer API itself was healthy.
alternatives.hypothesis: The 138 FAILED outbox events cause customer-visible transfer problems, such as missing downstream effects.

A.rule: no failed deliveries and pending stayed low
